questions.question: Explain the origin of emission and absorption spectral lines.
questions.solution_html: • Explain the origin of emission and absorption spectral lines. Ans. Spectral lines are obtained when electron jumps between discrete energy levels in atoms. Emission spectral lines appear when electrons jump from higher energy state to lower, emitting energy. The result is bright or coloured lines against a dark background. Absorption spectral lines occur when electrons make a transition from lower to higher energy level which is possible only by absorbing energy. The result is dark lines in bright background because that energy has been absorbed. Ans. (1 mark) for each. /
questions.final_answer: Explain the origin of emission and absorption spectral lines. Ans. Spectral lines are obtained when electron jumps between discrete energy levels in atoms. Emission spectral lines appear when electrons jump from higher energy state to lower, emitting energy. The result is bright or coloured lines against a dark background. Absorption spectral lines occur when electrons make a transition from lower to higher energy level which is possible only by absorbing energy. The result is dark lines in bright background because that energy has been absorbed. Ans. for each.

questions.question: Discuss the process of energy absorption and emission in an atom.
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the process of energy absorption and emission in an atom. /
  • Ans: There are two main ways in which an atom can be excited to an energy above its ground state and thereby
  • become able to radiate.
  • One of these ways is by a collision with another particle in which part of their joint kinetic energy is absorbed by the
  • atom.
  • Such an excited atom will return to its ground state in an average of 10−8𝑠 by emitting one or more photons.
  • Another excitation mechanism is involved when an atom absorbs a photon of light whose energy is just the right
  • amount to raise the atom to a higher energy level.
  • When white light, which contains all wavelengths, is passed through hydrogen gas, photons of those wavelength s that
  • correspond to transitions between energy levels are absorbed. The resulting excited hydrogen atoms reradiate their
  • excitation energy almost at once, but these photons come off in random directions with only a few in the same
  • direction as the original beam of white light. Any one method-2.5, both (5 marks)
  • Just mention 2 methods- (2 marks) . Pictorial representation only- (2 marks)
questions.final_answer: Just mention 2 methods- . Pictorial representation only

questions.question: Describe the process of population inversion and its role in the amplification of light in lasers. What methods are used to achieve it?
questions.solution_html:
• Describe the process of population inversion and its role in the amplification of light in lasers.What methods are
  • used to achieve it? /
  • Ans: The term population inversion describes an assembly of atoms in which the majority are in energy levels above
  • the ground state. (2 marks) .
  • If we can arrange this and then shine light of frequency on the assembly, there will be more stimulated emissions from
  • atoms in the metastable state than stimulated absorptions by atoms in the ground state. The result will be an
  • amplification of the original light. This is the concept that underlies the operation of the laser. (1 mark)
  • Any two methods to attain population inversion (pumping method) (2marks)
questions.final_answer: Any two methods to attain population inversion (pumping method)
